results.evidence: WTA's Chewuch River and Tungsten pages both route to Thirtymile via County Rd 1213 then FS Road 51, ~29 miles from Winthrop; Hiking Project's Chewuch #510 page gives the same FR 51 drive. The Forest Service / Trail Wiki Chewuch Trailhead listing places the 3900-300 spur 20 miles up FR 39 from Loomis, high-clearance only and not recommended until end of June — a different trailhead.

patches.find: The FS-39-300 spur to Chewuch Trailhead is maintained for high-clearance vehicles only and is not recommended for use until late June.

results.fact: Direction of the Boundary Trail leg and the summit slope
results.correct_value: Prose is right (Boundary Trail runs west from the mine camp ~1 mi, then bends south toward Apex Pass; summit climbed up the gentle west slopes). The 'Boundary Trail bend toward Apex Pass' pin (waypoints[5]) sits east of the mine camp and is misplaced — a coordinate fix, which is out of scope here.
results.evidence: Country Highpoints turned west on the Boundary Trail from the mine area and climbed Wolframite's gentle west slopes; SummitPost describes the west-side approach off the Boundary Trail near Apex Pass. The summit (lng -120.1296) is slightly east of the mine camp (-120.1323), so a mile west then northeast is geometrically consistent; only the pin's lat/lng disagrees.

SummitPost's Tungsten Mine Camp page puts the Chewuch #510 / Tungsten #534 intersection at ~4,700 ft. WTA's Tungsten page gives the trail as 6.2 mi, 2,100 ft gain, high point 6,800 ft, which places its lower end at ~4,700 ft. This matches the approach prose (~4,700 ft) and Day 2's 2,100 ft climb to the 6,750 ft camp.

Bivy-only dispute; bivy[] is owned by the camping clean-up. bivy[0] (Tungsten Creek trail camps below the junction) does serve this route but its note contradicts the itinerary's camp at Tungsten Mine Camp; bivy[1] (the mine camp itself) is the itinerary's camp and is hidden. No patch written.

season (Jul-Sep), best_season (mid-July through September), seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow (mid-July through September, October 'risky') and climate.bySeason.summer (mid-July through September) all agree; the variant's 'early October' is the lone outlier. Externally, the Country Highpoints October ascent met shin-deep snow on the approach and fresh snowfall on the summit.

The Trailhead waypoint says 3,400 ft while approach, approach_logistics.trailheadDirection, timing.sectionBreakdown[0] and itinerary day 1 all say ~3,600 ft. SummitPost gives ~3,600 ft; Hiking Project and Trailforks give the Chewuch trail's low point (the Thirtymile end) as ~3,430-3,440 ft. Sources disagree, so no patch.

results.evidence: The campsite (8.5 mi) and Tungsten Creek ford (8.7 mi) pins say 4,400 ft, only 0.1-0.3 mi before the junction now set at ~4,700 ft — a 300 ft jump the gentle Chewuch trail does not make. No source states either pin's elevation, so they are left for a ground check.
